independence_basis: separate process, fresh session, clean checkout, integrity verified

findings.evidence: _ROUTINE_CONFIG excludes remote.<r>.fetch/prune/mirror and branch.* from git_control_digest. integrate() runs `git fetch -q <remote> <target>`, and git updates the configured remote-tracking destination for the fetched ref. Probe /tmp/uri_review_R3/probe_fetch.py on the test fixture: the implementer worker runs `git -C <repo> config --add remote.origin.fetch +refs/heads/canon:refs/heads/session-b` and makes the real fix. Result at 39ed499: run() == COMPLETE, integration INTEGRATED, verify() == [], and refs/heads/session-b (another session's branch, with its own commit 3ee1d50) is force-moved to the baseline 16d4165. The same probe at 1f720ed (probe_fetch_old.py) stops BLOCKED with TAMPER 'git hooks or config changed during the repair', and session-b is untouched. The anchored control state (R1-04) and do_repair's ctl0 check both miss the change now. remote.<r>.mirror is also excluded; it makes the integration push fail (DoS only).
findings.suggested_fix: Remove remote.*.fetch (and mirror/prune/tagopt) from _ROUTINE_CONFIG, or at least run integrate's fetch with `--refmap=` (no opportunistic ref updates) and an explicit no-destination refspec, and add a regression test in which a worker-written fetch refspec is either TAMPER or provably cannot move any local ref. Keep the doc in sync.
findings.title: Config allowlist added in 39ed499 hides worker-written remote.*.fetch refspecs, which the driver's integration fetch then uses to force-overwrite other local branches of the main repository
